verdict.rationale: Isaac ROS packages are explicitly designed to run unmodified on both workstations and embedded Jetson hardware, and Isaac Sim's ROS 2 bridge lets the same ROS 2 stack that runs in simulation validate against real robot logic, implying code portability across sim/real. However, there is no explicit first-party claim or case study demonstrating identical robot application code running against both simulated and physical robots without modification. Missing for 10: an explicit sim-to-real code-parity guarantee/case study, and independent/hands-on confirmation that no rewrite is needed when switching from Isaac Sim to a real robot.
